packs.title: Ocean Explorers: Life Beneath the Waves
packs.subject: Ocean Science
packs.description: 20 original ocean questions on tides, reefs, marine life and science.

questions.question: What covers most of Earth's surface?
questions.explanation: Ocean water covers about seventy-one percent of Earth's surface.

questions.question: What causes most regular ocean tides?
options: The gravitational pull of the Moon, with a contribution from the Sun
questions.explanation: Lunar gravity dominates most tidal patterns.

questions.question: Why are coral reefs valuable?
options: They provide habitat for many marine species
They make all ocean water fresh
questions.explanation: Complex reefs shelter and support diverse organisms.

questions.question: What is a plankton organism?
options: A drifting organism carried by water movement
questions.explanation: Plankton includes small plants and animals that drift in water.

questions.question: What is phytoplankton's role in marine food webs?
options: It produces organic matter using light
questions.explanation: Many phytoplankton species perform photosynthesis.

questions.question: Which zone of the ocean receives the most sunlight?
questions.explanation: Light generally decreases as water depth increases.

questions.question: Why does ocean water taste salty?
options: It is mixed with sand only
questions.explanation: Weathering and other processes supply dissolved salts to the ocean.

questions.question: Which marine animal is a mammal?
questions.explanation: Dolphins breathe air and nurse their young.

questions.question: How do many fish obtain dissolved oxygen?
questions.explanation: Fish gills exchange gases with surrounding water.

questions.question: What does a marine protected area try to do?
questions.explanation: Protection rules can help preserve marine ecosystems.

questions.question: How can plastic litter affect sea turtles?
options: Turtles may mistake plastic for food or become entangled
questions.explanation: Ingestion and entanglement are serious risks.

questions.question: What is an estuary?
options: A place where river water mixes with seawater
questions.explanation: Estuaries contain a changing mixture of fresh and salt water.

questions.question: Why do mangrove forests help young fish?
options: Their roots create sheltered nursery habitats
They are made only of coral
questions.explanation: Many juvenile fish use sheltered mangrove waters.

questions.question: What is sonar commonly used for?
options: Using sound waves to detect objects underwater
questions.explanation: Sound travels well underwater and can reveal submerged objects.

questions.question: What is the deep ocean usually like?
options: Filled with sunlight at all depths
Cold, dark and under high pressure
questions.explanation: Deep water has little light and can have high pressure.

questions.question: What are ocean currents?
questions.explanation: Currents transport water, heat and nutrients.

questions.question: What is a sustainable seafood choice concerned with?
options: Avoiding unnecessary harm to fish populations and habitats
questions.explanation: Fishing practices affect marine ecosystems and future stocks.

questions.question: Why can fertiliser runoff damage coastal water?
options: Excess nutrients may trigger harmful algal blooms
questions.explanation: Too many nutrients can cause blooms and oxygen problems.

questions.question: What is a scientific use of an underwater robot?
options: Explore places difficult or dangerous for divers
questions.explanation: Remotely operated vehicles collect images and measurements.

questions.question: How can students help protect nearby beaches?
options: Take litter home and join safe clean-up efforts
Leave fishing lines in the sand
Release plastic packaging into the sea
questions.explanation: Reducing litter helps protect coastal habitats.

packs.title: Engineering Workshop: Build & Test
packs.subject: Engineering
packs.description: 20 engineering design and physics questions about structures, testing and inventions.

questions.question: What is the first useful step in an engineering project?
questions.explanation: Clear requirements guide a practical design.

questions.question: Why do engineers build models?
options: To test ideas before constructing full-size designs
questions.explanation: Models help reveal strengths and weaknesses.

questions.question: Why are triangles common in bridge trusses?
options: They can form rigid structures that distribute loads
They remove the need for materials
questions.explanation: Triangular geometry can improve structural stability.

questions.question: What is a load in structural engineering?
options: A force or weight acting on a structure
questions.explanation: A load is something a structure must support.

questions.question: What does a lever help a person do?
options: Change the effort or direction needed to move a load
questions.explanation: Levers provide mechanical advantage in suitable arrangements.

questions.question: Why is a safety factor used in design?
options: To make every structure heavier without purpose
To guarantee that nothing can fail
To account for uncertainty and unexpected stresses
questions.explanation: Safety factors allow margins beyond expected loads.

questions.question: What is friction?
options: A force resisting relative motion between surfaces
questions.explanation: Friction acts against sliding or attempted sliding.

questions.question: Which material is commonly used for electrical insulation?
questions.explanation: Rubber generally resists electrical current.

questions.question: Why does a bicycle need brakes?
options: To slow and stop through controlled friction
questions.explanation: Brakes dissipate motion energy, often as heat.

questions.question: What is a renewable energy engineering challenge?
options: Storing electricity when the wind is not blowing
questions.explanation: Energy storage helps balance variable renewable generation.

questions.question: A bridge prototype bends too far in a test. What should the team do?
options: Review the load path and revise its design
questions.explanation: Tests should inform design changes.

questions.question: What is the role of a gear?
options: Transmit rotation and change speed or torque
questions.explanation: Gears transfer turning motion between shafts.

questions.question: What does an engineer mean by an iteration?
options: A design that can never change
A revised version after learning from a test
questions.explanation: Iteration improves a design through repeated cycles.

questions.question: Why must drinking-water systems be carefully designed?
options: To deliver water safely and reduce contamination risk
To maximise colour in the pipes
questions.explanation: Public water systems need safe treatment and distribution.

questions.question: What is a sensor in a robot?
options: A device that measures conditions or detects changes
questions.explanation: Sensors supply information to a control system.

questions.question: Why is accessibility important in building design?
options: People with different mobility and sensory needs should be able to use spaces
Only one body size should be considered
questions.explanation: Inclusive design aims to remove barriers.

questions.question: What does a pulley system do?
options: Change the direction of a force and sometimes reduce effort
questions.explanation: Pulleys can offer mechanical advantage.

questions.question: Why do engineers record measurements during tests?
options: To compare actual performance with requirements
questions.explanation: Recorded data supports evidence-based decisions.

questions.question: What is a trade-off in design?
options: Improving one feature may require sacrificing another
questions.explanation: Designs must balance several competing requirements.

questions.question: Which action shows good workshop safety?
options: Wear suitable eye protection and follow tool instructions
Leave sharp tools on the floor
questions.explanation: Protective equipment and safe procedures reduce risk.

packs.title: World Cultures & Traditions
packs.subject: World Cultures
packs.description: 20 cross-cultural questions on languages, traditions, food and respectful exchange.

questions.question: Why is it useful to learn greetings in another language?
options: It can help show respect and start conversations
It makes every person speak English
questions.explanation: Trying another language can build connection and respect.

questions.question: What does cultural diversity mean?
options: Different cultural practices and experiences existing together
Everyone having exactly the same traditions
questions.explanation: Diversity describes variation among communities.

questions.question: Which Malaysian festival is widely associated with decorative kolam designs?
questions.explanation: Kolam patterns are often displayed for Deepavali celebrations.

questions.question: What is a common element of Chinese New Year celebrations?
questions.explanation: Reunion meals and visits are important for many families.

questions.question: Which celebration marks the end of Ramadan for Muslims?
questions.explanation: Aidilfitri follows the Ramadan fasting month.

questions.question: What does the term 'heritage' often include?
options: Traditions, objects and knowledge passed between generations
questions.explanation: Cultural heritage can be tangible or intangible.

questions.question: Why should visitors ask before photographing a cultural ceremony?
options: Some people or activities require permission and respect
Cameras always take better photos at night
questions.explanation: Asking helps respect privacy and local customs.

questions.question: What is an oral tradition?
options: Stories or knowledge shared through speaking
questions.explanation: Communities can pass knowledge verbally.

questions.question: Which instrument is associated with the Malaysian gamelan tradition?
questions.explanation: Gamelan ensembles use instruments including gongs and metallophones.

questions.question: What does a traditional recipe often teach about a place?
questions.explanation: Food reflects resources, migration and community practices.

questions.question: Why is respectful disagreement important in intercultural discussions?
options: People may have different beliefs and experiences
questions.explanation: Respectful dialogue allows different perspectives.

questions.question: What is an example of intangible cultural heritage?
options: A traditional dance performed across generations
questions.explanation: Performances and skills can be intangible heritage.

questions.question: What is a 'dialect' in language?
options: A regional or social variety of a language
A language that cannot be spoken
questions.explanation: Dialects vary in pronunciation, vocabulary or grammar.

questions.question: Which festival is celebrated in parts of Sabah by Kadazan-Dusun communities?
questions.explanation: Kaamatan is associated with harvest celebrations in Sabah.

questions.question: What is a cultural stereotype?
options: An oversimplified belief about a whole group
A reliable description of every individual
questions.explanation: Stereotypes ignore differences between individuals.

questions.question: Why should museums describe where artefacts came from?
options: Provenance provides historical and ethical context
questions.explanation: Provenance helps explain origins and ownership.

questions.question: What does bilingual mean?
questions.explanation: Bilingual people use two languages to varying degrees.

questions.question: What can music across cultures reveal?
options: Different rhythms, instruments and social functions
That every song has the same beat
questions.explanation: Music expresses creativity and community traditions.

questions.question: Which practice supports cultural exchange?
options: Listening, asking respectful questions and sharing knowledge
questions.explanation: Exchange works better with curiosity and mutual respect.

questions.question: Why might a traditional craft be taught to younger people?
options: To stop people learning other crafts
To preserve skills and allow creative adaptation
questions.explanation: Transmission can sustain heritage while allowing change.

packs.title: Communities, Citizenship & Public Services
packs.subject: Civics
packs.description: 20 non-partisan questions about communities, public services, shared rules and responsibility.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a public library?
options: Provide access to books, information and learning resources
questions.explanation: Libraries support education and community access.

questions.question: Why do communities have traffic rules?
options: To reduce crashes and coordinate road use
questions.explanation: Shared rules improve predictability and safety.

questions.question: What does 'public service' commonly refer to?
options: Services intended to benefit the community
questions.explanation: Public services support shared needs.

questions.question: Why should school rules be clear and accessible?
options: Only teachers need to know them
Students can understand expectations and apply them fairly
questions.explanation: Clear rules help people act consistently.

questions.question: What is volunteering?
options: Giving time or effort to help others without expecting wages
questions.explanation: Volunteers support community activities.

questions.question: Why are emergency exits clearly marked?
options: People need a route to safety during an emergency
To replace building maps for all uses
questions.explanation: Visible exit signs assist evacuation.

questions.question: What is a community consultation?
options: An opportunity for residents to share views on a proposal
questions.explanation: Consultations collect perspectives on decisions.

questions.question: How should a disagreement about a shared playground be handled?
options: Discuss needs and seek a fair practical solution
questions.explanation: Listening and compromise can resolve shared-space disputes.

questions.question: Why do towns collect household waste?
options: To replace recycling with dumping everywhere
To maintain sanitation and manage materials safely
questions.explanation: Waste services reduce public health and environmental risks.

questions.question: What is a pedestrian crossing for?
options: Helping people cross roads in a designated place
questions.explanation: Crossings organise vehicle and pedestrian movement.

questions.question: Which practice shows responsible digital citizenship?
options: Create false accounts to harass classmates
Respect others and avoid sharing private information without permission
questions.explanation: Good digital citizenship combines respect and privacy.

questions.question: Why are local parks important?
options: They can offer recreation and support urban nature
They guarantee every city has identical weather
questions.explanation: Parks provide opportunities for play and green space.

questions.question: What does fairness in a classroom involve?
options: Applying rules consistently while considering relevant needs
questions.explanation: Fair decisions need consistency and reasonable accommodation.

questions.question: What is a useful way to report a broken streetlight?
options: Notify the appropriate local service with its location
questions.explanation: Accurate reports help services identify the problem.

questions.question: What is a local community group?
options: People cooperating around a shared neighbourhood or interest
questions.explanation: Groups coordinate activities and mutual support.

questions.question: Why should public information be written clearly?
options: Residents need to understand services and instructions
questions.explanation: Accessible language helps more people use information.

questions.question: What should someone do if they find a lost wallet at school?
options: Give it to a trusted staff member
questions.explanation: Staff can handle lost property safely.

questions.question: Why is listening important in group decisions?
options: It helps reveal needs and concerns that others may have
questions.explanation: Listening can lead to more informed decisions.

questions.question: What is a shared community resource?
options: Something residents use or benefit from together
questions.explanation: Libraries, parks and pathways are examples of shared resources.

questions.question: Which action demonstrates care for public facilities?
options: Use equipment responsibly and report damage
questions.explanation: Responsible use helps facilities remain available to others.
